name: Action and Response
summary: A thought becomes action. The motor cortex generates precise movement commands, refined by the cerebellum.
description: The premotor cortex plans the sequence of movements. The primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus) then fires specific motor neurons corresponding to the muscles needed — each body part mapped onto the motor homunculus. The cerebellum provides real-time error correction, comparing intended movements with actual feedback. The basal ganglia act as a gate — they inhibit unwanted movements and release desired ones. Parkinson's disease, caused by dopamine loss in the basal ganglia, makes it difficult to initiate movements. Deciding not to act — inhibiting an impulse — is itself an active neural process requiring prefrontal suppression of motor commands.
